filename: Machine-learned Cloud Classes from Satellite data for Process-oriented Climate Model Evaluation.pdf
title: Machine-learned Cloud Classes from Satellite data for Process-oriented Climate Model Evaluation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
testbed_rationale: The study develops a diagnostic framework for process-oriented climate model evaluation of cloud types rather than a training benchmark dataset or testbed for building ML parameterizations.
pain_points: Severe class imbalance in satellite cloud types (e.g., very few Stratus and Deep Convection samples; Cumulus and Cirrus underestimated).
Standard climate model output (e.g., CMIP6) typically lacks instantaneous values and key cloud optical/microphysical variables (e.g., cloud optical thickness, liquid and ice effective radii).
Model performance breaks down when applied to temporally averaged (e.g., monthly mean) data instead of instantaneous/near-instantaneous data.
Distinguishing Stratus from Stratocumulus is difficult due to sensor footprint limitations and similar physical characteristics.
Passive sensor satellite retrievals have high uncertainties in high-latitude/polar regions (e.g., Greenland, Antarctica) and difficulty assessing thermodynamic phase in mixed-phase clouds.
Scaling Random Forests to hundreds of millions of samples requires heavy subsampling due to memory constraints; CNN replacements failed to converge.
extraction_notes: The primary ML task involves pixel-level classification (IResNet semisupervised CNN) followed by coarse-resolution multivariate fractional regression (Random Forest) predicting 9-class fractional distributions (8 WMO cloud types plus undetermined/clear-sky).
